title: MORE Words and Phrases
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; illustrated music translations suggested separately

entries.example: Jack is her boyfriend.
entries.description: A boy who a girl loves

entries.example: This is my band. Its name is Project 11.
entries.description: The dog is hungry. ___ bowl is empty.

entries.example: They play the guitar.
entries.description: To do this with toys, games or a guitar

entries.example: This is my sister.
entries.description: A girl in your family who has the same parents as you

entries.example: She can play the drums. He can't sing.
entries.description: Fish ___ swim, but they ___ fly.

entries.example: Let's go to the concert tomorrow.
entries.description: A show where a band plays music

entries.example: Let's dance to the music!
entries.description: To move your body to music
You say this to tell someone that everything is OK

entries.example: She has a good job.
entries.description: The work that a person does for money

entries.example: The job is perfect for you.
entries.description: Very, very good, with nothing wrong

entries.example: Can you carry my guitar?
entries.description: To hold something and take it with you

entries.example: I can stand on my head.
entries.description: To have your feet on something

entries.example: He can touch his nose with his tongue.
entries.description: It is pink and in your mouth; you taste with it

entries.example: Please don't touch my guitar.
entries.description: To put your hand or finger on something

entries.example: Can you walk on your hands?
entries.description: To go step by step on something

entries.example: He can wiggle his ears.
entries.description: To move something quickly from side to side

entries.example: Look, he carries fifteen cans.
entries.description: A metal thing for drinks like cola

entries.example: I can't drink fifteen cans.
entries.description: To have water or juice

entries.example: Can you eat a hundred apples?
Can you drink five cans in one go?
entries.description: All at once, without a break
You say this when you are surprised and want to know if it's true
You point at a photo of yourself and say it

entries.example: The economy is the world of money.
entries.description: The world of money, work and business

entries.example: The Clown Doctors go to hospitals and help children.
entries.description: A place where doctors help sick people

entries.example: They make children laugh.
entries.description: What you do when something is very funny

entries.example: I get my pocket money from my mum and dad.
entries.description: What you get from your parents every week to buy things

entries.example: A cup of apple juice is 2 pounds.
entries.description: Money in England

entries.example: It's 120 pounds. That's my profit.
entries.description: The money you make when you sell more than you pay

entries.example: We have apple juice in our school canteen.
entries.description: The room where pupils eat lunch during the day

entries.example: I put a table in our playground.
entries.description: You eat your meals at it

entries.example: Mr Davis is my teacher at school.
entries.description: A person who works at a school and gives lessons

entries.example: My uncle is my dad's brother.
entries.description: Your father's or mother's brother

entries.example: I wash my mum's car.
entries.description: To make something clean with water and soap

entries.example: There's nothing in the garden.
entries.description: Not anything; zero things
You say this when you didn't hear what someone said
The musician in a band who hits things with sticks
The musician who blows into a big golden jazz instrument
A person who plays an instrument with six strings
The musician in a band who makes music with keys like a piano
An instrument you hit with sticks
A golden instrument you blow into, popular in jazz
The person in a band who uses their voice to make music
An electric piano
